summary: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated remote-controlled PTY/SSH agent with server-pushed self-update
details: The package's sole runtime is dist/index.cjs, a 14 MB obfuscator.io bundle (rotating 109,104-entry string array, _0xXXXX identifiers, control-flow flattening) that main and the whalent-core bin both point at. The bundle imports ssh2 and node-pty and references WebSocket, Authorization, /task, /heartbeat, onData, and process.env.SHELL, wiring a remote WebSocket peer to a local pseudo-terminal/shell on the installer's host — a network-to-PTY control channel that yields arbitrary command execution on the machine that installs or runs the package. The bundle also contains an updateAgent symbol and the README documents that the package 'is replaced by remote daemon upgrades', so the whalent server can push replacement code into every deployed instance. Whoever controls that server has persistent full-host command execution on installers, and the heavy obfuscation of the only shipped runtime prevents verification of which server is trusted or which commands are accepted.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
